evidence.pali: 208 . ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, evaṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati byāpādavitakko…pe… uppajjati vihiṃsāvitakko. So evaṃ pajānāmi – ‘uppanno kho me ayaṃ vihiṃsāvitakko. So ca kho attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattaniko’. ‘Attabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘parabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘ubhayabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattaniko’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, uppannuppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ pajahameva vinodameva byantameva naṃ akāsiṃ.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 208. “诸比丘，当我如此不放逸、热忱、自我策励地安住时，生起了瞋寻……乃至……生起了害寻。我这样了知：‘我生起了这个害寻。它既导致恼害自己，也导致恼害他人，还导致恼害双方；它障碍智慧，是苦恼品类，不导向涅槃。’诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害自己’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害他人’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害双方’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它障碍智慧，是苦恼品类，不导向涅槃’时，它就消失了。诸比丘，我就是这样，对每一个生起的害寻，都予以舍断、去除、灭尽。”
evidence.english: 208. “Monks, as I was dwelling thus—heedful, ardent, and resolute—a thought of ill will arose in me… a thought of violence arose in me. I understood it thus: ‘This thought of violence has arisen in me. It leads to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; it obstructs wisdom, is on the side of distress, and does not lead to Nibbāna.’ As I reflected, ‘It leads to my own affliction,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It leads to the affliction of others,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It leads to the affliction of both,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It obstructs wisdom, is on the side of distress, and does not lead to Nibbāna,’ it subsided in me. Monks, I would abandon, dispel, and make an end of each thought of violence as it arose.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: 181 . Tatiyachakke kāmo ti dve kāmā – vatthukāmo ca kilesakāmo ca. Tattha kilesakāmaṃ sandhāya kāmapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu kāmadhātu, kāmavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vatthukāmaṃ sandhāya kāmoyeva dhātu kāmadhātu, kāmāvacaradhammānametaṃ nāmaṃ. Byāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu byāpādadhātu, byāpādavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Byāpādova dhātu byāpādadhātu, dasaāghātavatthukassa paṭighassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vihiṃsā paṭisaṃyuttā dhātu vihiṃsādhātu, vihiṃsāvitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vihiṃsāyeva dhātu vihiṃsādhātu, parasattavihesanassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Ayaṃ pana heṭṭhā anāgatattā evaṃ atthādivibhāgato veditabbā – vihiṃsanti etāya satte, vihiṃsanaṃ vā etaṃ sattānanti vihiṃsā. Sā viheṭhanalakkhaṇā, karuṇāpaṭipakkhalakkhaṇā vā; parasantāne ubbegajananarasā, sakasantāne karuṇāviddhaṃsanarasā vā; dukkhāyatanapaccupaṭṭhānā; paṭighapadaṭṭhānāti veditabbā. Nekkhammaṃ vuccati lobhā nikkhantattā alobho, nīvaraṇehi nikkhantattā paṭhamajjhānaṃ, sabbākusalehi nikkhantattā sabbakusalaṃ. Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu nekkhammadhātu, nekkhammavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Nekkhammameva dhātu nekkhammadhātu, sabbassāpi kusalassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu abyāpādadhātu, abyāpādavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Abyāpādova dhātu abyāpādadhātu, mettāyetaṃ nāmaṃ. Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu avihiṃsādhātu, avihiṃsā vitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Avihiṃsāva dhātu avihiṃsādhātu, karuṇāyetaṃ nāmaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 181. 于第三组六界中，欲有两种：事欲(vatthukāma)与烦恼欲(kilesakāma)。其中，与烦恼欲相应的界为欲界，此是欲寻之名。与事欲相应者，欲本身即是界，为欲界，此是欲界诸法之名。与瞋相应的界为瞋界，此是瞋寻之名。瞋本身即是界，为瞋界，此是十愤恨事之名。与害相应的界为害界，此是害寻之名。害本身即是界，为害界，此是恼害他有情之名。此“害”因前文未述，故当从义理等方面作此分别：以其伤害有情，或对有情的伤害，故为“害”。其特征为恼害，或与悲相反；作用为于他人生起怖畏，或于自身毁坏悲心；现起为苦的依处；近因为瞋，当如是了知。出离，因出离贪欲，故为无贪；因出离诸盖，故为初禅；因出离一切不善法，故为一切善法。与出离相应的界为出离界，此是出离寻之名。出离本身即是界，为出离界，此是一切善法之名。与无瞋相应的界为无瞋界，此是无瞋寻之名。无瞋本身即是界，为无瞋界，此是慈之名。与无害相应的界为无害界，此是无害寻之名。无害本身即是界，为无害界，此是悲之名。
entries.english: 181. In the third set of six, 'sensual desire' (kāma) refers to two kinds of sensual desire: sensual objects (vatthukāma) and defilement-sensual desire (kilesakāma). Herein, with reference to defilement-sensual desire, the element associated with sensual desire is the sensual-desire element (kāmadhātu); this is a name for sensual thought (kāmavitakka). With reference to sensual objects, the element that is simply sensual desire is the sensual-desire element; this is a name for phenomena of the sense-sphere (kāmāvacaradhammā). The element associated with ill will is the ill-will element (byāpādadhātu); this is a name for ill-will thought (byāpādavitakka). The element that is simply ill will is the ill-will element; this is a name for aversion (paṭigha) based on the ten grounds for anger (dasa āghātavatthu). The element associated with cruelty is the cruelty element (vihiṃsādhātu); this is a name for cruelty thought (vihiṃsāvitakka). The element that is simply cruelty is the cruelty element; this is a name for the tormenting of other beings (parasattavihesana). This, however, as it has not been mentioned before, should be understood by way of its division into meaning, and so forth: 'vihiṃsā' means that by which beings are harmed, or it is the harming of beings. It has the characteristic of injuring, or the characteristic of being the antithesis of compassion; its function is to generate agitation in the continuity of others, or to destroy compassion in one's own continuity; it manifests as a basis for suffering; and it has aversion (paṭigha) as its proximate cause. 'Renunciation' (nekkhamma) is said to be non-greed because of having departed from greed, the first jhāna because of having departed from the hindrances, and all that is wholesome because of having departed from all that is unwholesome. The element associated with renunciation is the renunciation element (nekkhammadhātu); this is a name for renunciation thought (nekkhammavitakka). The element that is simply renunciation is the renunciation element; this is a name for all that is wholesome (sabbakusala). The element associated with non-ill-will is the non-ill-will element (abyāpādadhātu); this is a name for non-ill-will thought (abyāpādavitakka). The element that is simply non-ill-will is the non-ill-will element; this is a name for loving-kindness (mettā). The element associated with non-cruelty is the non-cruelty element (avihiṃsādhātu); this is a name for non-cruelty thought (avihiṃsāvitakka). The element that is simply non-cruelty is the non-cruelty element; this is a name for compassion (karuṇā).

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Sammāsaṅkappa niddese kāmato nissaṭoti nekkhammasaṅkappo . Byāpādato nissaṭoti abyāpādasaṅkappo . Vihiṃsāya nissaṭoti avihiṃsāsaṅkappo . Tattha nekkhammavitakko kāmavitakkassa padaghātaṃ padacchedaṃ karonto uppajjati, abyāpādavitakko byāpādavitakkassa, avihiṃsāvitakko vihiṃsāvitakkassa. Nekkhammavitakko ca kāmavitakkassa paccanīko hutvā uppajjati, abyāpādaavihiṃsāvitakkā byāpādavihiṃsāvitakkānaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 在正思惟的解释中，‘离于欲’即出离寻，‘离于嗔’即无嗔寻，‘离于害’即无害寻。于此，出离寻生起时，截断、破除欲寻；无嗔寻截断嗔寻；无害寻截断害寻。出离寻作为欲寻的对治法而生起，无嗔寻与无害寻亦作为嗔寻与害寻的对立面而生起。
entries.english: In the exposition of right intention: The thought of renunciation is that which has emerged from sensual desire. The thought of non-ill-will is that which has emerged from ill-will. The thought of non-harming is that which has emerged from harm. Herein, the thought of renunciation arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of sensual desire; the thought of non-ill-will arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of ill-will; and the thought of non-harming arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of harm. The thought of renunciation arises as an opponent to the thought of sensual desire, and the thoughts of non-ill-will and non-harming arise as opponents to the thoughts of ill-will and harm.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: Tattha yogāvacaro kāmavitakkassa padaghātanatthaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ vā sammasati aññaṃ vā pana kiñci saṅkhāraṃ. Athassa vipassanākkhaṇe vipassanāsampayutto saṅkappo tadaṅgavasena kāmavitakkassa padaghātaṃ padacchedaṃ karonto uppajjati, vipassanaṃ ussukkāpetvā maggaṃ pāpeti. Athassa maggakkhaṇe maggasampayutto saṅkappo samucchedavasena kāmavitakkassa padaghātaṃ padacchedaṃ karonto uppajjati; byāpādavitakkassāpi padaghātanatthaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ vā aññaṃ vā saṅkhāraṃ sammasati; vihiṃsāvitakkassa padaghātanatthaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ vā aññaṃ vā saṅkhāraṃ sammasati. Athassa vipassanākkhaṇeti sabbaṃ purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于此，行者为断除欲寻，或思择欲寻，或思择其他某行。其后，于观之刹那，与观相应的思惟以支分断的方式断除、破斥欲寻而生起，策励观而令至道。其后，于道之刹那，与道相应的思惟以正断的方式断除、破斥欲寻而生起。为断除嗔寻，亦或思择嗔寻，或思择其他行；为断除害寻，亦或思择害寻，或思择其他行。其后‘于观之刹那’等，一切皆应如前述而组合。
entries.english: Herein, the yogi reflects on the thought of sensual desire or any other formation in order to strike at the thought of sensual desire. Then, at the moment of insight, the thought associated with insight arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of sensual desire by way of temporary suppression, and having intensified insight, it leads to the path. Then, at the moment of the path, the thought associated with the path arises, striking at and cutting off the thought of sensual desire by way of complete eradication. Similarly, to strike at the thought of ill-will, one reflects on the thought of ill-will or any other formation; to strike at the thought of harm, one reflects on the thought of harm or any other formation. Then, at the moment of insight, everything should be applied in the same way as before.

entries.pali: 182 . Ubhayattha uppanno ti sattesu, saṅkhāresūti ubhayattha uppanno, sattākāro, saṅkhārākāroti vā ārammaṇassa ubhayākāraggahaṇavasena uppanno. Kammapathaviseso, kammapathavināsako ca kammapathabhedoti dassetuṃ ‘‘abhijjhāsaṃyogenā’’ tiādi vuttaṃ. Tathā vihiṃsāya vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ dassetīti yojanā. Vihiṃsāyā ti ca vihiṃsāvacanenāti attho. Yathāsambhavaṃ pāṇātipātādivasenā ti ādi -saddena adinnādānamusāvādapesuññapharusavācāsamphappalāpe saṅgaṇhāti. Sabba…pe… saṅgāhakehi kāmanekkhammadhātūhi. Dve dve ti byāpādavihiṃsādhātuyo, abyāpādaavihiṃsādhātuyo ca. ‘‘Etthāti panā’’ tiādinā saṃkilesavodānānaṃ saṅkarabhāvassa aniṭṭhāpajjanassa ca dassanena purimaṃyeva atthaṃ byatirekamukhena sampādeti.
entries.chinese_simplified: 182. “于二者中生起”(ubhayattha uppanno)，即于众生与诸行中生起；或作众生相、诸行相，或因执取所缘的二相而生起。为了显示业道的差别、业道的破坏者以及业道的类别，所以说了“以贪欲相应”(abhijjhāsaṃyogena)等。同样的，应连结为“以害(vihiṃsā)显示害寻(vihiṃsāvitakka)”。而“以害”(vihiṃsāya)意为“以害语”(vihiṃsāvacanena)。“以杀生等”(pāṇātipātādivasena)一句，其中的“等”字，随其可能，包含了不与取(adinnādāna)、妄语(musāvāda)、离间语(pesuñña)、粗恶语(pharusavācā)、绮语(samphappalāpa)。一切……乃至……被能摄的欲界与出离界所摄。两个两个的是指瞋恚界与害界，以及无瞋界与无害界。“在此……”(etthāti panā)等文，通过显示杂染和清净的混杂状态以及导致不欲之果，从而以否定的方式来确立前文的意义。
entries.english: 182. 'Arisen in both places' means arisen in both beings and formations; or, arisen as the aspect of beings and the aspect of formations; or, arisen by grasping the object in its dual aspects. To show the distinction, the destroyer, and the division of the course of action, it is said, 'by the connection with covetousness,' etc. Similarly, the connection is that it shows the thought of harming through harming. And 'through harming' means by the expression 'harming.' 'As appropriate, in the manner of killing living beings, etc.'—the word 'etc.' includes taking what is not given, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, and frivolous chatter. All... (the rest is omitted by 'pe') ...with the encompassing elements, namely, the elements of sensual desire and renunciation. 'Two and two' means the elements of ill will and harming, and the elements of non-ill will and non-harming. By 'But here,' etc., by showing the mingling of defilement and purification and the arising of the undesirable, it establishes the preceding meaning through the method of contrast.

entries.pali: Imesu tīsu ṭhānesū ti imesu viramitabbatāvasena jotitesu tīsu kāmabyāpādavihiṃsāvitakkavatthūsu. Visuṃ visuṃ uppannassa tividha akusalasaṅkappassa. Padapacchedato ti ettha gatamaggo ‘‘pada’’nti vuccati, yena ca upāyena kāraṇena kāmavitakko uppajjati, so tassa gatamaggoti tassa pacchedo ghāto padapacchedo, tato padapacchedato. Anuppattidhammatāpādanaṃ anuppattisādhanaṃ, tassa vasena. Maggakiccasādhanena maggaṅgaṃ pūrayamāno ekova tividhakiccasādhano kusalasaṅkappo uppajjati. Tividhākusalasaṅkappasamucchedanameva hettha tividhakiccasādhanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Iminā nayena ‘‘imesu catūsu ṭhānesū’’ tiādīsupi attho veditabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: ‘于此三处中’，指的是于此等应止息而阐明的三种欲、瞋、害寻事中。对于分别生起的三种不善思惟而言。所谓‘断径’(padapaccheda)，此处‘径’(pada)指所行之道。欲寻通过何种方法、何种原因生起，那便是它的所行之道；切断、破坏此道，即是‘断径’。因此，说‘从断径’。使之具有不生起的性质，即是成就其不生起，依此之故。以成办道的作用来圆满道支时，能成办三种作用的唯一善思惟(kusalasaṅkappa)就会生起。此处应当明白，断除三种不善思惟本身，即是成办三种作用。依此理趣，‘于此四处’等语句的含义也应当这样理解。
entries.english: ‘In these three places’ means in these three bases for sensual, hostile, and harmful thoughts, which are indicated as things to be refrained from. Regarding the individually arisen threefold unwholesome thought. ‘From cutting off the path’: here, the course taken is called ‘pada’; and the means or cause by which a sensual thought arises is its course. The cutting off or destruction of that is ‘padapaccheda’; hence, ‘from cutting off the path.’ Bringing about the state of non-arising is the accomplishment of non-arising; by means of that. Fulfilling the path factor by accomplishing the function of the path, a single wholesome thought arises that accomplishes the threefold function. Here, the accomplishment of the threefold function should be understood as precisely the complete eradication of the threefold unwholesome thought. By this method, the meaning should also be understood in phrases such as 'in these four places.'

entries.pali: 188 . ‘‘Tathā tatheva gadanato’’ ti iminā ‘‘tathāgato’’ti āmeḍitalopenāyaṃ niddesoti dasseti. Tathā tathevā ti ca dhammaatthasabhāvānurūpaṃ, veneyyajjhāsayānurūpañcāti adhippāyo. Diṭṭhanti rūpāyatanaṃ daṭṭhabbato, tena yaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, yaṃ dissati, yaṃ dakkhati, yaṃ sati samavāye passeyyaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ ‘‘diṭṭhaṃ’’ tveva gahitaṃ kālavisesassa anāmaṭṭhabhāvato. ‘‘Suta’’ ntiādīsupi eseva nayo. Sutanti saddāyatanaṃ sotabbato. Muta nti sanissayena ghānādiindriyena sayaṃ patvā pāpuṇitvā gahetabbaṃ. Tenāha ‘‘patvā gahetabbato’’ ti. Viññāta nti vijānitabbaṃ, taṃ pana diṭṭhādivinimuttaṃ viññeyyanti āha ‘‘sukhadukkhādidhammāyatana’’ nti. Patta nti yathā tathā pattaṃ, hatthagataṃ adhigatanti attho. Tenāha ‘‘pariyesitvā vā apariyesitvā vā’’ ti. Pariyesita nti pattiyāmatthaṃ pariyiṭṭhaṃ, taṃ pana pattaṃ vā siyā appattaṃ vā ubhayathāpi pariyesitamevāti āha ‘‘pattaṃ vā appattaṃ vā’’ ti. Padadvayenāpi dvippakārampi pattaṃ, dvippakārampi pariyesitaṃ, tena tena pakārena tathāgatena abhisambuddhanti dasseti. Cittena anusañcarita nti copanaṃ apāpetvā citteneva anusaṃcaritaṃ, parivitakkitanti attho. Pītakanti ādī ti ādi -saddena lohitakaodātādi sabbaṃ rūpārammaṇavibhāgaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Sumano ti rāgavasena, lobhavasena, saddhādivasena vā sumano. Dummano ti byāpādavitakkavasena, vihiṃsāvitakkavasena vā dummano. Majjhatto ti aññāṇavasena vā ñāṇavasena vā majjhatto. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Tattha tattha ādi -saddena saṅkhasaddo paṇavasaddo, pattagandho pupphagandho, pattaraso phalaraso, upādinnaṃ anupādinnaṃ, majjhattavedanā kusalakammaṃ akusalakammanti evaṃ ādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 188. ‘如其所如而言说故’，以此显示‘如来’(tathāgato)一词是经由叠词省略而作的解释(niddesa)。‘如其所如’的意趣是，既符合法的义理与自性，也符合所教化者的意乐。‘所见’(diṭṭha)，指色处(rūpāyatana)，因其可被见；由此，凡是已见、正见、当见，或当因缘和合时可见者，皆总括为‘所见’，因其不涉及时间的差别。‘所闻’(suta)等也是同样的道理。‘所闻’，指声处(saddāyatana)，因其可被听。‘所觉’(muta)，指依靠鼻根等感官，自身到达、触及而领受者。因此说‘因触及而领受故’。‘所识’(viññāta)，指应被识知者；但它是有别于所见等的所知，因此说‘苦、乐等法处(dhammāyatana)’。‘所得’(patta)，指如其所得，意即到手、已证得。因此说‘或经由遍求，或未经遍求’。‘所遍求’(pariyesita)，指为得而遍求；此或已得，或未得，两种情况都名为‘所遍求’，因此说‘或已得，或未得’。此二词显示了两种‘所得’与两种‘所遍求’，如来通过这些方式完全证悟。‘以心随行’，指不令（身）动，仅以心随行，意即思量。‘黄色’等，此中‘等’字，总括了红色、白色等一切色所缘的分别。‘悦意’(sumano)，指因贪欲、贪婪或信心等而心悦。‘不悦’(dummano)，指因瞋寻或害寻而心不悦。‘中舍’(majjhatto)，指因无知或智慧而住于中舍。此理于一切处皆然。各处所说‘等’字，当知总括了螺声、鼓声，叶香、花香，叶味、果味，有取、无取，舍受，善业、不善业等。
entries.english: 188. "Thus, indeed, by speaking" — this shows that the designation "Tathāgata" is indicated through the elision of repetition. "Thus, indeed" means in accordance with the nature of the Dhamma and its meaning, and in accordance with the disposition of those to be taught — this is the intention. "Seen" refers to the visible object, as it is to be seen. Whatever was seen, whatever is seen, whatever will be seen, whatever one might see when the conditions are present — all that is included under "seen," because the distinction of time is not considered. The same applies to "heard," etc. "Heard" refers to the audible object, as it is to be heard. "Sensed" refers to what is to be grasped by the faculty of smell, etc., along with its basis, by reaching and attaining it directly. Hence it is said, "by reaching and grasping." "Known" refers to what is to be cognized. But this is distinct from the seen, heard, and sensed, so it is called "the knowable," referring to the objects of mind such as pleasure and pain. "Attained" means attained in whatever way, come to hand, acquired. Hence it is said, "whether sought after or not sought after." "Sought after" means searched for the sake of attainment. Whether attained or not attained, both are still "sought after." Thus, by these two terms, two kinds of attainment and two kinds of seeking are shown, indicating how the Tathāgata has fully awakened to them in every way. "Traversed by mind" means traversed by the mind alone, without agitation—that is, pondered. "Yellow, etc." — the word "etc." includes all divisions of visible objects, such as red, white, etc. "Glad" means joyful due to lust, greed, faith, etc. "Sorrowful" means distressed due to ill will, harmful thoughts, etc. "Neutral" means indifferent due to ignorance or knowledge. The same applies everywhere. Here, the word "etc." should be understood to include sounds like conch-shells and drums, smells like leaf-scents and flower-scents, tastes like leaf-tastes and fruit-tastes, the clung-to and the unclung-to, neutral feeling, wholesome and unwholesome kamma, and so forth.

entries.pali: 16 . Yenā ti asubhādīnaṃ anussaraṇalakkhaṇena indriyena taṇhāmayitavatthūsu kāmataṇhāya sahajātaṃ vitakkaṃ vāreti, idaṃ asubhādianussaraṇalakkhaṇaṃ indriyaṃ satindriyaṃ. Yena mahaggatabhāvappattena avikkhepena byāpādavitakkaṃ vāreti, idaṃ avikkhepasaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ samādhindriyaṃ. Yena sammappadhānena vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ vāreti, idaṃ sammappadhānasaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ. Yena sammādiṭṭhisaṅkhātena indriyena uppannuppanne…pe… nādhivāseti, idaṃ sammādiṭṭhisaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ paññindriyaṃ . Imesu catūsu indriyesu saha uppajjamānā yā saddahanā okappanā uppajjati, anāvilabhāvato idaṃ saddahanasaṅkhātaṃ indriyaṃ saddhindriyaṃ . Imāni sekkhassa pañcindriyāni.
entries.chinese_simplified: 16. 以不净等随念为相的根，能于渴爱所染之事中，防止与欲贪俱生的寻(vitakka)，此以不净等随念为相的根，即是念根。以已达广大(mahaggata)状态的不散乱，能防止瞋恚寻，此被称为不散乱的根，即是定根。以正勤(sammappadhāna)，能防止加害寻，此被称为正勤的根，即是精进根。以被称为正见的根，于已生已生（的恶法）……不忍受，此被称为正见的根，即是慧根。于此四根中，当俱时生起的信解、胜解生起时，因其无浊的状态，此被称为信解的根，即是信根。这些是有学的五根。
entries.english: 16. That faculty which, by its characteristic of recollecting the unattractive and so forth, restrains the thought co-arisen with sensual craving regarding objects of craving—this faculty, with its characteristic of recollecting the unattractive and so forth, is the faculty of mindfulness. That faculty which, by the non-distraction that has attained a sublime state, restrains the thought of ill will—this faculty, designated as non-distraction, is the faculty of concentration. That faculty which, by right effort, restrains the thought of harmfulness—this faculty, designated as right effort, is the faculty of energy. That faculty which, by the faculty designated as right view, does not tolerate arisen... this faculty, designated as right view, is the faculty of wisdom. Among these four faculties, the conviction and trust that arise simultaneously—due to its unclouded nature—this faculty, designated as conviction, is the faculty of faith. These are the five faculties of a trainee.

entries.pali: Akusalapakkhena ‘‘arakkhitena cittenā’’ ti padena vutto asaṃvaro ‘‘cakkhuasaṃvaro …pe… kāyaasaṃvaro, copanakāyaasaṃvaro, vācāasaṃvaro, manoasaṃvaro’’ti aṭṭhavidhena vibhajitabbo. ‘‘Micchādiṭṭhihatenā’’ ti padena gahito micchāsaṅkappo ‘‘kāmavitakko byāpādavitakko vihiṃsāvitakko’’ti tividhena vibhajitabbo. ‘‘Micchādiṭṭhī’’ ti padena vuttā micchādiṭṭhi ‘‘dukkhe aññāṇaṃ…pe…idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppannesu dhammesu aññāṇa’’nti aṭṭhavidhena vibhajitabbā, dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhividhenapi vibhajitabbā. Thinamiddhaṃ pañcavidhena sasaṅkhārikavidhena vibhajitabbaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 在不善品中，‘以无守护心(arakkhitena cittenā)’一词所说的不防护(asaṃvara)，应分为八种：‘眼不防护(cakkhuasaṃvara)……乃至身不防护(kāyaasaṃvara)、触动身不防护(copanakāyaasaṃvara)、语不防护(vācāasaṃvara)、意不防护(manoasaṃvara)’。‘以邪见所害(micchādiṭṭhihatenā)’一词所摄的邪思惟(micchāsaṅkappa)，应分为三种：‘欲寻思(kāmavitakka)、嗔寻思(byāpādavitakka)、害寻思(vihiṃsāvitakka)’。‘邪见(micchādiṭṭhi)’一词所说的邪见，应分为八种：‘于苦无智、于苦集无智、于苦灭无智、于趣苦灭之道无智、于前际无智、于后际无智、于前后际无智、于此缘性缘起法无智’，也应以六十二见(dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhi)的方式分析。昏沉睡眠(thinamiddha)应以五种有行(sasaṅkhārika)的方式分析。
entries.english: On the unwholesome side: non-restraint, mentioned by the term 'with an unguarded mind,' should be analyzed in eight ways: 'non-restraint of the eye ... non-restraint of the body, non-restraint of bodily agitation, non-restraint of speech, non-restraint of mind.' Wrong intention, which is taken by the term 'slain by wrong view,' should be analyzed in three ways: 'sensual thought, thought of ill will, and thought of cruelty.' Wrong view, mentioned by the term 'wrong view,' should be analyzed in eight ways: 'ignorance regarding suffering ... ignorance regarding dhammas that are dependently arisen based on specific conditionality'; it should also be analyzed in sixty-two ways according to the kinds of views. Sloth and torpor should be analyzed in five ways, by the classification of that which is prompted.

entries.pali: ‘‘Katamaṃ, mahārāja, bhagavato samādhiratanaṃ? Savitakkasavicāro samādhi, avitakkavicāramatto samādhi, avitakkaavicāro samādhi, suññato samādhi, animitto samādhi, appaṇihito samādhi. Samādhiratanaṃ kho, mahārāja, piḷandhassa bhikkhuno ye te kāmavitakkabyāpādavitakkavihiṃsāvitakkamānuddhaccadiṭṭhivicikicchākilesavatthūni vividhāni ca kuvitakkāni, te sabbe samādhiṃ āsajja vikiranti vidhamanti viddhaṃsanti na saṇṭhanti na saṇṭhahanti (sī.) na upalimpanti na upalippanti (sī. pī.) . Yathā, mahārāja, vāri pokkharapatte vikirati vidhamati viddhaṃsati na saṇṭhāti na upalimpati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Parisuddhattā padumassa. Evameva kho, mahārāja, samādhiratanaṃ piḷandhassa bhikkhuno ye te kāmavitakkabyāpādavitakkavihiṃsāvitakkamānuddhacca diṭṭhivicikicchākilesavatthūni vividhāni ca kuvitakkāni, te sabbe samādhiṃ āsajja vikiranti vidhamanti viddhaṃsanti na saṇṭhanti na upalimpanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Parisuddhattā samādhissa. Idaṃ vuccati, mahārāja, ‘bhagavato samādhiratana’nti, evarūpāni kho, mahārāja, samādhiratanāni bhagavato ratanāpaṇe pasāritāni.
entries.chinese_simplified: “大王，什么是世尊的定宝？有寻有伺定，无寻唯伺定，无寻无伺定，空定，无相定，无愿定。大王，对于佩戴定宝的比丘来说，那些欲寻、嗔寻、害寻、慢、掉举、邪见、疑等诸种烦恼事，以及种种不善的寻思，一接触到定，就都会消散、瓦解、毁灭，不能停留，不能染着。大王，就像水落在荷叶上，会流散、瓦解、毁灭，不能停留，不能染着。这是什么原因呢？因为莲花是清净的。同样地，大王，对于佩戴定宝的比丘来说，那些欲寻、嗔寻、害寻、慢、掉举、邪见、疑等诸种烦恼事，以及种种不善的寻思，一接触到定，就都会消散、瓦解、毁灭，不能停留，不能染着。这是什么原因呢？因为定是清净的。大王，这被称为‘世尊的定宝’。大王，像这样种种的定宝，都在世尊的珍宝店中陈列着。”
entries.english: “Great king, what is the Blessed One’s jewel of concentration? Concentration with initial and sustained application, concentration without initial application but with sustained application, concentration without initial or sustained application, the emptiness concentration, the signless concentration, and the undirected concentration. For a monk adorned with the jewel of concentration, great king, all those various bases of defilement—sensual thoughts, thoughts of ill-will, thoughts of harm, conceit, restlessness, wrong views, and doubt—and various unwholesome thoughts, upon encountering concentration, are scattered, dispersed, and destroyed; they do not settle, they do not adhere. Just as, great king, water on a lotus leaf is scattered, dispersed, and destroyed; it does not settle, it does not adhere. For what reason? Because of the purity of the lotus. In the same way, great king, for a monk adorned with the jewel of concentration, all those various bases of defilement—sensual thoughts, thoughts of ill-will, thoughts of harm, conceit, restlessness, wrong views, and doubt—and various unwholesome thoughts, upon encountering concentration, are scattered, dispersed, and destroyed; they do not settle, they do not adhere. For what reason? Because of the purity of concentration. This, great king, is called ‘the Blessed One’s jewel of concentration.’ Such, great king, are the jewels of concentration displayed in the Blessed One’s jewel shop.”
